instructions.content: Prefer one root config unless migration constraints require nested overrides
Keep lint and format authority singular for each file path
Optimise for deterministic CI (read-only checks) and reproducible local fixes
Confirm prerequisites first: an Nx workspace, Node.js 18+ and a selected package manager
Install Biome and initialise the root configuration (root biome.json exists)
Add project targets (or plugin inferred tasks) and enable Nx caching inputs
Validate lint and format execution on one project, then run across the workspace with run-many
Apply a migration strategy: all-at-once, or selective with nested biome.json or scoped overrides
NEVER use nested biome.json for simple workspace-wide setups; use one root config and add nested configs only for migration or real overrides
NEVER run ESLint and Biome on the same files without an explicit boundary; each file set has one active lint authority
NEVER omit biome.json and the Biome dependency from Nx cache inputs; include "{workspaceRoot}/biome.json" and externalDependencies ["@biomejs/biome"]
NEVER auto-enable formatter writes in CI verification jobs; use check or lint mode in CI and reserve write mode for local or dedicated fix jobs
NEVER downgrade critical Biome rules to suppress migration noise; scope temporary exceptions narrowly with documented expiration
Run nx reset after plugin changes so the daemon cache clears and targets refresh
Do not use the skill when the repository intentionally standardises on ESLint and Prettier only, or when the task is not Nx-related
